Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (962 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you watch the Bundesliga, then you'll know Wael Mohya is a fast-footed, quick-thinking footballer.
  • "Of course, I was absolutely thrilled.
  • "And the fact that it's come to this now is, of course, just awesome and makes me very proud.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you watch the Bundesliga, then you'll know Wael Mohya is a fast-footed, quick-thinking footballer. But not even the 17-year-old (Mohya turns 18 on December 31) Borussia Mönchengladbach youngster would have expected to be called up to the Germany squad so soon.

"Of course, I was absolutely thrilled. It means a great, great deal to me. I think everyone dreams of being selected for the national team at some point," Mohya said.

"And the fact that it's come to this now is, of course, just awesome and makes me very proud.".

Mohya was at the gym when the call came in. He then shared the good news with his parents over dinner. "They started crying," the teenager mentioned in a video posted on Gladbach's social media channels.

It has been revealed that the youngster, who was born in a small town east of Düsseldorf, smiles and laughs a lot in interviews. He is always friendly, and in a good mood. On the field, too, he exudes the lightheartedness and carefree spirit of a 17-year-old.

As a technically skilled and creative player, Mohya often seeks out one-on-one situations and puts his opponents under pressure with quick dribbles. In nine Bundesliga appearances this season, Mohya has scored twice and delivered one assist.

In a recent development, "He's so cool and just plays really well. It's fun to watch him," Borussia coach Alexander Blessin said recently.

It has been revealed that "Wael brings a lot to the team with his laid-back attitude on the field. He's not afraid to take risks, no matter how much pressure there is," added Gladbach's sporting director Rouven Schröder at a talk show on Sport1.

Borussia Mönchengladbach has been Mohya's sporting home since he was seven years old. Last season, previous head coach Eugen Polanski promoted him to the first team, and in December 2025, Mohya made his Bundesliga debut. Against Wolfsburg, aged 16 years and 347 days old, he became the youngest Bundesliga player in the club's history.

Sources indicate that mohya also recently completed a voluntary social year at an elementary school in Mönchengladbach. This is a program in Germany for young people who volunteer in the social sector — at hospitals, schools, or nursing homes, for example — for about six to 18 months. They gain work experience, help others, and earn a little money.

At the school's open all-day care program, Mohya helped serve meals, assisted children with their homework, and played with them. That's also where his nickname comes from. Because a girl hadn't understood his first name correctly or couldn't pronounce it, she called him "Waffel." Now, that name has stuck.

Industry observers note that even before being called up to the Germany team, clubs in the Bundesliga and across Europe's top leagues had taken notice of Mohya and were trying to sign him. His contract with Borussia Mönchengladbach runs through 2028.

With Gladbach at the moment in a relegation battle, his future appears likely to be elsewhere. If the club wants to generate transfer revenue from its biggest talent, next summer would likely be the opportunity to sell him — unless he extends his contract with Borussia.

Recent findings suggest that the 17-year-old's career is managed by his parents. Whichever club can convince them that their son is in good hands and help him reach his full potential likely has the best chance of securing Mohya's signing.

Mohya himself says he doesn't even know how much he's right now earning at Gladbach.

"My parents take care of all that," he told Bild recently. "I get a monthly allowance, which is more than enough for me.".

Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp recently revealed how much he had enjoyed his conversations with the youngster.

"The conversations I had with him were great," Klopp said with a laugh. "I wasn't that confident at 17, but then again, I wasn't that good either.".

It has been revealed that since Mohya's parents are from Morocco, their son also holds Moroccan citizenship. As a result, he could have played for Morocco, but he has now decided against it. In fact, the Moroccan football association had been actively courting Mohya as early as last year and had already reached out to him in the run-up to the 2026 World Cup.

Now, like Frankfurt's Younes Ebnoutalib, Mohya will continue to play in the German jersey, unlike Schalke's Soufiane El-Faouzi, who chose Morocco, or Bayer Leverkusen's Ibrahim Maza, who likely would have been selected by Klopp as well if he hadn't already opted for Algeria.

For Mohya, who played for Germany's youth teams from the U16s through to the U21s, the door to Morocco remains open, even if he does play for Germany. According to FIFA regulations, players under the age of 21 can change national teams before their fourth international match (whether a competitive or friendly match), provided that none of those matches take place during a World Cup or a continental tournament such as the European Championship, Copa America, or Africa Cup of Nations.

If Mohya plays in the upcoming UEFA Nations League games in Serbia or against the Netherlands, another record is on the horizon. Although there were two even younger players who made their debuts in the Germany jersey — Willy Baumgärtner in 1908 (at 17 years and 104 days) and Marius Hiller in 1910 (at 17 years and 241 days) — the era in which they debuted is hardly comparable. And so, while Wael Mohya would rank third overall on the list, he would become the youngest Germany player in the modern era. The youngest to date was Hamburg legend Uwe Seeler in 1954, aged 17 years and 345 days.

#71614. The last golden era of the Premier League is long gone: Why 2004-16 was the best of the Barclays

The last golden era of the Premier League is long gone: Why 2004-16 was the best of the Barclays

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1102 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fourfourtwo

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the so-called “Best League in the World™”, it’s safe to say the Premier League is currently experiencing a full-blown existential crisis.
  • The bombshell announcement of Manchester City’s guilt on all but one of their 115 charges has left the game feeling more hollow than ever before.
  • So with that, let’s cast our minds to a simpler, purer time, the much-fabled “Barclays era” of 2004 to 2016.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the so-called “Best League in the World™”, it’s safe to say the Premier League is currently experiencing a full-blown existential crisis.

The bombshell announcement of Manchester City’s guilt on all but one of their 115 charges has left the game feeling more hollow than ever before. Is there a title race? Who’s going down? What is real? Does any of this mean anything? Throw in the continued abomination that is VAR and more, and it’s all just a bit bleak.

So with that, let’s cast our minds to a simpler, purer time, the much-fabled “Barclays era” of 2004 to 2016.

While football didn’t start in 1992, the Premier League did and by the early-to-mid 2000s, it was reaching its apex as the blood and thunder of decades prior fused with the upcoming-found flair and panache to create a near-perfect concoction.

The current state of the English top-flight can be traced all the way back to the summer of 2003 with Roman Abramovich’s purchase of Chelsea. It was the moment the horse bolted and nothing has been the same since.

However, at the time, it was all just a little bit exciting and things really picked up 12 months later when Jose Mourinho landed in West London, rightly claiming to be the “Special One”. The reigning European Cup winner was joined by Rafael Benitez, who came to Liverpool after incredible success with Valencia.

Suddenly, Sir Alex Ferguson and Arsene Wenger were no longer the only gunslingers in town. The “Big Two” quickly became the “Big Four” as Mourinho romped to the league title - breaking numerous records - and Benitez amazingly won the Champions League. Istanbul and all that.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

According to recent reports, the two Iberians changed so much in the English game. From how to set up a side to how to win the title - 4-4-2 and peaking after Christmas being swapped out for 4-3-3 and rapid-fast starts.

It has been revealed that liverpool’s fifth European Cup was significant for numerous reasons. It was their first in 21 years but also the first final featuring an English side in the 21st century. They had beaten Chelsea to get there, starting both an incredible rivalry between the clubs and managers, and a golden age for the Premier League.

Over the next four years, all of the then-”Big Four” made finals and there were three semi-finalists in every season from 06/07 to 08/09. The peak came in 2008 when each was knocked out by another with United eventually toppling Chelsea in the first all-English final in Moscow. In one of the odder paradoxes, England failed to qualify for the European Championships that summer.

Recent findings suggest that fergie’s empire had struck back with Cristiano Ronaldo and Wayne Rooney at the forefront of it. In an era of elite pairings, there was no finer. Ronaldo’s Ballon d’Or win confirmed his status as the best player in the world, and the Premier League as truly the best league.

It was also a time of far less financial disparity with the rest of Europe, Milan and Inter lifting the Champions League in 2007 and 2010 respectively. Things would soon change and not for the better.

While the massive boys competed for the biggest trophies, there were plenty of brilliant stories elsewhere. Harry Redknapp’s Portsmouth won the FA Cup in 2008, setting the tone for Wigan five years later in epic fashion against City months on from Swansea claiming the League Cup. Only Crystal Palace's success in 2025 has been comparable since.

Throw in Big Sam’s Bolton, Blackburn, Stoke, Hull and others and it was the last definitive age of the cult teams and cult heroes, or as they’ve become better known - The Barclaysmen. With the overload of data nowadays, another Michu-like madness feels further away than ever.

Abu Dhabi’s takeover of City in 2008 is the obvious place to pinpoint the beginning of the end, but Mourinho’s first Chelsea exit a year prior and Ronaldo’s first from United a year after moved the centre of attention from England to Spain.

In a recent development, while European success faded - a fate-like Chelsea were the only winners from 2008 to 2019 - there were still memorable domestic moments, two of which unfortunately led to City winning their first pair of Premier League titles. Agueroooooo and Gerrard’s slip may be rendered utterly irrelevant soon but the memories won’t. It was peak Premier League.

Sources indicate that as was Sir Alex Ferguson’s last dance in 2013 and Leicester’s miracle title win in 2016, which will never be topped as the greatest achievement in the history of English football. That it came either side of Chelsea’s crooked titles and prior to City’s dodgy dominance makes it all the more appropriate as the ending of the last great era. And that goes for both in football and the world itself.

While the on-field action of the last decade may feel fraudulent, how we now consume football is also a far cry from those halcyon Barclays days.

Industry observers note that streaming was not yet a thing in 2004. Sky Sports was in its pomp. Super Sunday actually lived up to its billing as appointment viewing.

Influencers and content creators had not yet taken over. Gary Neville went past his winger on the overlap rather than host it. Social media was still fun for the most part.

We had Soccer AM and Goals on Sunday, Gillette Soccer Saturday and Match of the Day at elite levels, and even room for shows like Wayne Rooney’s Street Striker and Football’s Next Star.

Nostalgia is a helluva drug, but as Independent Panels decide the fate of English football past, present and future, it’s near-impossible to dispute that, like so much of entertainment, we had it so much better before.

One day, the pendulum will hopefully swing back in our favour but, for now, a rewatch of Premier League Years on Sky may be in order.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, tenerife won 5-2 at Badajoz in the Copa del Rey despite finishing the match with ten men.
  • At the Estadio Nuevo Vivero on Wednesday 18 November, Álvaro Cervera’s side booked a place in the second round of the Copa del Rey.
  • Cervera started a line-up made up largely of reserves.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, tenerife won 5-2 at Badajoz in the Copa del Rey despite finishing the match with ten men. The victory keeps their cup run alive ahead of the second-round draw.

At the Estadio Nuevo Vivero on Wednesday 18 November, Álvaro Cervera’s side booked a place in the second round of the Copa del Rey. The tie had been postponed twice, first after the train accident in Toledo province and then after the death of Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel on 3 November, who was remembered with a minute’s silence.

Cervera started a line-up made up largely of reserves. It still produced a scoreline Tenerife had never recorded in 260 Copa del Rey matches, according to elDiario.es (Canarias Ahora). About 3,000 spectators watched, around 20 per cent of the stadium’s capacity.

Grant-Leon Ranos opened the scoring in the sixth minute from a Marc Mateu assist. Juanjo Sánchez added a second a minute later. Ranos struck again in the 38th minute, set up by Gerard Valentín.

According to recent reports, carlos Beitia pulled one back for Badajoz in the 49th minute. Roko Jureškin was then sent off in the 58th minute. Ten-man Tenerife still extended the lead through substitute Iván Chapela in the 69th minute, assisted by Martin Pečar.

Jorge Barba replied for the hosts in the 74th minute from a Manuel Hernández assist. Víctor Moreno completed the scoring deep into stoppage time, with Álvarez providing the pass.

It has been revealed that the Segunda Federación side went into the tie third in their group. They were also unbeaten in seven league matches in a row.

In a recent development, tenerife have now come through their opening Copa del Rey tie in eight seasons in a row. The win followed a 2-0 victory over AD Ceuta FC. Before that came a run of draws against FC Andorra, Sabadell, Celta de Vigo II and Girona.

This was the first meeting between the clubs in the cup. They had played each other 22 times in Segunda División. Tenerife won ten of those games, Badajoz eight, and four ended level. Tenerife’s previous visit to Badajoz, on 30 March 2003, ended in a 2-1 defeat under David Amaral.

Cervera’s side return to league duty at home to Mallorca in Segunda División on Saturday 21 November. Badajoz travel to Recreativo Huelva in Segunda División RFEF Group 4 on Sunday 22 November.

The second round will feature 56 teams in 28 one-off ties. The lower-division side hosts if its ground meets federation standards. The draw was put back because of the postponed first-round matches. The Ciudad del Fútbol in Las Rozas, Madrid, home of the federation, is the venue for it.

#71610. Inside Gotham FC's move to Icahn Stadium: Debates over pitch quality, fines and the NWSL's logistical struggle

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2207 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

Inside Gotham FC's move to Icahn Stadium: Debates over pitch quality, fines and the NWSL's logistical struggle

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2207 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that juan Carlos Amoros is always subtle in demeanor, down to his usual all-black attire, so after Gotham FC's uninspiring 1-0 win over the Seattle Reign on Sunday, his subdued tone was hardly a surprise.
  • "I feel the obligation to almost apologize for the state of the pitch," Amoros said.
  • Sources indicate that he was hardly the only one to mention the grass at Sports Illustrated Stadium.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that juan Carlos Amoros is always subtle in demeanor, down to his usual all-black attire, so after Gotham FC's uninspiring 1-0 win over the Seattle Reign on Sunday, his subdued tone was hardly a surprise. His post-match remarks, though, were a departure from the victory lap a coach might take after winning in the NWSL quarterfinals.

"I feel the obligation to almost apologize for the state of the pitch," Amoros said. "I think at this level, in this kind of game, as a league, we should be having a better surface. Unfortunately, our football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn't but luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt and the game was what it was.".

Sources indicate that he was hardly the only one to mention the grass at Sports Illustrated Stadium. It seeped its way into every post-match media availability, dominated conversation between the players and was a talking point amongst staff working that day. A dull stretch of grass with yellow-green splotches overshadowed one of the most vital matches of the NWSL's season – and put the league on course for an unlikely downsize for Sunday's playoff semifinal between Gotham and the Kansas City Current.

According to recent reports, roughly 24 hours after Amoros' apology, Gotham moved Sunday's game to Icahn Stadium, a 5,000-seater on Manhattan's Randall's Island that they have played at just twice before. Sports Illustrated Stadium, the 25,000-seat venue in Harrison, N.J. that Gotham have called home since 2021, was available but concerns about player safety prompted an unwanted last-minute move.

"We as a team worked extremely hard to earn a home playoff berth," Gotham captain Tierna Davidson remarked in a statement on Monday. "What we got was a field that is not the standard this club, this league or our fans deserve. The quality of the game is not up for debate, so we've made the difficult decision to move to Icahn Stadium on Sunday. A smaller stadium means many of you will not be there, and that is the hardest part of this decision.".

Monday's announcement was the final stage of a back-and-forth between Gotham and MLS' Red Bull Fresh York, the primary tenants and operators of Sports Illustrated Stadium, one that highlights the logistical nightmares that have unexpectedly disrupted the NWSL's postseason.

MLS' World Cup break this summer afforded RBNY the chance to install a new pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, the process complete by the team's July 25 loss to Charlotte FC. It was the perfect time for a reset ahead of a busy schedule for the new field – 17 other matches were a guarantee, while the potential postseason runs for both RBNY and Gotham meant the number could stretch well over 20 games before the year was over.

By the time Gotham had secured a home quarterfinal with a draw against Angel City on Oct. 4, there was little reason to suspect that the playing surface would become an concern. Matches are rarely relocated because of pitch quality concerns and the field at Sports Illustrated Stadium has historically been one of American soccer's best; it won the Sports Turf Management Association's award for professional soccer fields in 2021, the year Gotham moved in. The NWSL team did not have another home game until Nov. 1, a period in which RBNY played three home games and the stadium hosted a USA Rugby Fall Series doubleheader. Sometime before the early November fixture against the Royals, Gotham raised concerns with their landlords about the field conditions, the scars of the rugby games on Oct. 30 notably visible.

Nothing came of those complaints, though, and so the Royals match went on as scheduled but the conditions did not go unnoticed. The NWSL imposed a $10,000 fine on Gotham for the state of the field, even though they do not manage the venue as secondary tenants. The fine was not widely known – the NWSL Players Association mentioned it was unaware of the punishment, while a source with knowledge of the matter said RBNY also did not know. Many found out about the fine after Reign head coach Laura Harvey mentioned it in a post-match press conference after the quarterfinal, but worry about the quality of the grass had already reached a fever pitch at that point.

Despite the fine, a field consultant working on the NWSL's behalf inspected the pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium on Friday and declared that it met FIFA standards. The following day, RBNY hosted their regular season finale against Atlanta United and less than 18 hours later, another group took a look at the field in the hours building up to Gotham's win over the Reign. It was deemed playable on Sunday morning by representatives from the NWSL, the Professional Referee Organization and the NWSLPA, according to a source familiar with the situation.

Even from a distance, the grass appeared problematic. The sand that was left over from the rugby doubleheader still lined the pitch, while some rugby lines were faint but visible in certain spots. The players' review of the surface, though, was damning – Harvey called it "s---," Reign captain Jess Fishlock said it was "atrocious," and Gotham midfielder Jaelin Howell described it as "sandy" and "unstable." Gotham attacker Jaedyn Shaw also expressed concern that her planted foot would slip during corner kicks and all agreed that it ultimately impacted the teams' ability to compete.

lower bowl isn’t quite full at kickoff between Gotham and the Seattle Reign, though there are some fans in the upper bowlGotham announced earlier that they sold 3,000 tickets through NYC Mayor Mamdani’s offer (including 1,000 in the first 10 minutes of sale)#NWSL pic.twitter.com/qviBM65bsz.

Gotham, in conjunction with the NWSL, spent the hours after their quarterfinal win discussing options with RBNY to improve the playing surface. The main solutions, according to multiple sources, were re-sodding the pitch – essentially ripping the existing field out and installing a latest one – or a hybrid model in which artificial threads would be stitched into the existing grass. Both would be timely endeavors – the former would be longer while the latter might have been completed in time for Gotham to host the Current on Sunday.

There was just one problem. RBNY have a friendly against Club America scheduled for Saturday.

The game will serve as the final match of their season after they missed the MLS Cup playoffs and takes place during the men's international break, which means some players from both teams will be tied up with their national teams instead. Multiple sources noted the NWSL could not guarantee that the hybrid model project would not actually be completed in time for RBNY's friendly on Saturday evening, even if it would have been ready in time for Gotham's Sunday afternoon game against the Current. RBNY were unwilling to proceed with the hybrid plan, as a result, and so Gotham chose to leave Sports Illustrated Stadium for Icahn Stadium.

RBNY still intend to play on the pitch that NWSL players complained about on Saturday and no changes to the field are expected to be made beforehand.

"We understand how frustrating the move is for Gotham and their fans. We had hoped to see Gotham continue its championship run at Sports Illustrated Stadium, too," RBNY remarked in a statement. "We invest in the pitch year-round, with a dedicated grounds team and specialist field partners, and it was cleared for every match played there this season. Those inspections continue for all remaining events this year. We worked closely with Gotham and the NWSL to address their concerns, but unfortunately the experts and the league couldn't guarantee the additional work they wanted to be completed could be done in time. We wish Gotham the best in their match.".

The venue is not brand new to Gotham, who have hosted two games at the stadium in the last two years, and seems well-equipped to at least solve the main problem they faced at Sports Illustrated Stadium. Amoros complimented the quality of Icahn Stadium's pitch when Gotham hosted a Concacaf W Champions Cup group stage game there in Aug. 2025. Though it did not prompt Gotham's selection of Icahn Stadium to host that match, the New Jersey venue's field had also looked suboptimal in the run-up to the continental clash. RBNY subsequently replaced the pitch during that period, weeks before the U.S. men's national team played a friendly against South Korea on Sept. 6 last year.

"I don't really want to talk too much about it but the Sports Illustrated Stadium has traditionally been the best pitch in the league," Amoros said at the time, "and the last couple of games, it's definitely been far away from that so this pitch here is outstanding.".

Gotham's last-minute switch to Icahn Stadium was a surprise in large part because an entirely separate scheduling matter had overshadowed the first week of the postseason.

Sources indicate that the NWSL had two broadcast slots for the semifinals, Saturday at noon ET on CBS and Sunday at 3 p.m. ET on ABC, but did not exactly have the first-choice venues to host them. RBNY's Saturday friendly locked Gotham out of that time slot entirely if they wanted to play at Sports Illustrated Stadium, but they needed the Washington Spirit to beat the Portland Thorns for the Sunday window since the Thorns would be unable to hold a game that kicked off at 9 a.m. local time. The Spirit's lopsided win guaranteed Gotham would play on Sunday but they had their own complications – the Secretaries' Cup, a Division III college football game between the United States Merchant Marine Academy and the United States Coast Guard Academy, was taking place at Audi Field during the Saturday time slot.

The Spirit seemed destined for a semifinal at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Md., home of the NFL's Washington Commanders and a stadium they had never played in before, but late discussions with Audi Field's owners, MLS' D.C. United, and a contribution from sponsor Lafayette Federal Credit Union to underwrite the costs of the schedule change meant that problem was solved.

Recent findings suggest that gotham's move to Icahn Stadium, though, only reinforced the logistical challenges that the NWSL has battled for its entire existence. The optics have favored the league in recent years, with the vast majority of their teams playing in state-of-the-art soccer-specific stadiums and managing to survive the constant game of venue Tetris. Scheduling conflicts, though, were never out of the realm of possibility, and many have marred the league this year. The Boston Legacy, for example, had to move home games from Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Mass. to Centreville Bank Stadium in Pawtucket, R.I., during the World Cup and will play there in 2027 while the construction project continues on Boston's White Stadium.

Industry observers note that the issues that plagued Gotham and the Spirit, though, are in line with a different problem – control over facilities. Around half of the league's teams are secondary tenants in the stadiums they play in, so management of the venues is almost entirely out of their hands. It is unclear how quickly that will change for any of those teams. Gotham will leave Sports Illustrated Stadium for Etihad Park in 2028, but that stadium will be managed by MLS' New York City FC. They will continue to be secondary tenants in that building, which technically means they could be subject to the same problems they at the moment face. MLS' calendar flip next year will likely see the matter morph but not necessarily change. The leagues' postseason schedules will be different for the foreseeable future but teams like Gotham and the Spirit will still be at the mercy of their landlords in the meantime; Gotham's conflict with RBNY an example of just that. RBNY's friendly was the sticking point in their discussions over the pitch and ultimately took precedence over an NWSL semifinal.

It has been revealed that control over venues continues to weigh heavily in the NWSL's expansion process and is a key part of the matter that causes the most hand-wringing in the league's front office – the calendar. The Current might be the NWSL's gold standard as the owners and operators of CPKC Stadium, though they have been hamstrung by the NWSL's scheduling complications. Kickoff of their quarterfinal win over Angel City was at 11:30 a.m. local time because they were the only team able to take that broadcast slot on CBS. The since-ousted San Diego Wave could not host a game with a 9:30 a.m. local kickoff, while Gotham and the Spirit were locked out of their venues because of MLS matches on the same day.

It has been revealed that there is a meet-in-the-middle approach, one that the NWSL might use as often as they can as the expansion process continues. A handful of teams share ownership groups with MLS teams, who chiefly own and operate their own stadiums and tend to treat the NWSL teams as equal tenants. The number will grow in 2028 when teams in Atlanta and Columbus, both owned by the local MLS clubs, will join the league.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Real Madrid have extended the contracts of Aurélien Tchouaméni and Arda Güler until June 2032, a day apart.
  • Recent findings suggest that real Madrid have committed two midfield regulars to long-term deals in the space of 24 hours.
  • In a recent development, both players are part of the core of Mourinho’s midfield.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Real Madrid have extended the contracts of Aurélien Tchouaméni and Arda Güler until June 2032, a day apart. With captain Fede Valverde also reportedly agreeing new terms, the club are securing its core midfield for years to come.

Recent findings suggest that real Madrid have committed two midfield regulars to long-term deals in the space of 24 hours. Güler’s announcement came first, and Aurélien Tchouaméni’s followed.

In a recent development, both players are part of the core of Mourinho’s midfield. The renewals keep them at the club for six more seasons.

Tchouaméni arrived in 2022 and has made 205 appearances for the club. He has won eight trophies in that time. They include one Champions League, two Club World Cups and two UEFA Super Cups. He has also lifted one LaLiga, one Copa del Rey and one Spanish Super Cup.

His standing goes beyond the club. He has 50 France caps and won the 2021 Nations League. The new contract is worth around €9 million net per season, GOAL reported. The agreement came after interest from Manchester United.

Güler’s record covers a shorter spell. He was 18 when he joined. He has 38 caps for Turkey. In September he was named Breakthrough Player of the 2025-26 Champions League. His newly introduced salary is reportedly about €8m a year.

The two profiles differ. Tchouaméni is an established international with a full set of club honours. Güler is a younger player whose contract now runs almost nine years from his arrival. Tying both to the same end date suggests a midfield the club intend to keep together.

Sources indicate that the club may not be finished. Captain Fede Valverde has agreed to extend his contract from 2029 to 2031, according to GOAL. The newly introduced deal will make him one of the squad’s highest earners. An announcement is expected soon, as Madrid work on further renewals after Güler and Tchouaméni.

#71604. Tech Report: Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?

Tech Report: Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1052 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For members of the Indigenous Sasak community on the Indonesian island of Lombok, the conflict over their land is not over.
  • For them, a tourism and infrastructure project co-financed by the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is a source of frustration, as they believe it has led to the expropriation of their land and destruction of their livelihoods.
  • In late September, they officially filed a complaint with the bank.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For members of the Indigenous Sasak community on the Indonesian island of Lombok, the conflict over their land is not over.

For them, a tourism and infrastructure project co-financed by the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is a source of frustration, as they believe it has led to the expropriation of their land and destruction of their livelihoods.

In late September, they officially filed a complaint with the bank. It remains unclear whether this complaint will lead to an independent investigation.

The AIIB, which finances major infrastructure projects across Asia, has a mechanism in place to deal with such complaints.

Individuals who suffer adverse effects from the bank-financed projects may, under certain conditions, file a complaint with the institution.

However, access to this process — known as the Project Complaints Mechanism (PPM) — remains controversial.

According to a report by The Diplomat, a magazine that covers political and economic developments in Asia, none of the 45 complaints listed on the AIIB's website had been deemed admissible as of mid-September.

The bank acknowledged that "no cases have passed the PPM's eligibility assessment," but it stressed that this is "only part of the story.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The AIIB emphasized that not every problem needs to be resolved through this mechanism.

The PPM is "only one part of AIIB's grievance redress ecosystem," the Beijing-based bank said in response to a query from DW.

Those affected should first attempt to resolve concerns directly with the project team at the local level, it said.

According to the bank, "twelve complaints were in fact resolved at the project level — as a direct result of AIIB's follow-up and intervention — and one was resolved through domestic courts.".

But critics see this as a major weakness.

"The mechanism must be easily accessible," said Arntraud Hartmann, a development economist at the Johns Hopkins University School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS Europe) in Bologna, Italy.

In a recent development, she argued that people affected by the projects, for instance, are required to document potential violations of environmental and social standards from the start. "How is the affected party supposed to know which standards might have been violated?" she questioned.

It has been revealed that the AIIB disputes this claim. "In terms of accessibility, we have made the submission form simpler and translated it into 12 languages," it mentioned, adding that complaints can be submitted online, by phone, or by email.

Industry observers note that urgewald, a German environmental NGO, cites another problem with AIIB-financed projects. For many of them, information on environmental impacts and resettlements is either missing or published late, it noted.

Sources indicate that for 2024, the NGO found that 11 of the 16 projects it examined lacked complete environmental and social impact assessments. In many cases, information on the potential number of displaced residents was also missing, it added.

In a recent development, "The information published on the bank's website is often insufficient and inconsistent. Particularly key documents, such as environmental impact assessments or resettlement plans, vary widely or are missing entirely," noted Nora Sausmikat, a China expert at Urgewald.

The lack of information makes it difficult for those affected to respond promptly and report violations early on, she underscored, adding that the situation is particularly difficult for people without formal land titles.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Christoph Steinert, a political scientist at the University of Konstanz, stated the mere existence of such grievance redressal mechanisms "is not enough.".

Particularly vulnerable groups often know little about their rights, he said, adding that information should be available in local languages and targeted outreach directed at affected communities.

Criticism of the AIIB's procedures is not new. A 2023 report by international aid organizations, including Recourse, Accountability Counsel, and Inclusive Development International, revealed that the AIIB's grievance mechanism had failed to accept a single complaint since its 2019 inception.

The study highlighted that 101 of the 219 AIIB-financed projects, or 46% of the total projects at the time, were ineligible for review due to co-financing exemptions.

In a recent development, the AIIB typically provides funding without leading projects, a standard practice in development finance. When complaints arise, it directs complainants to the lead lender. As a result, nine of the 45 complaints fell outside its jurisdiction.

Industry observers note that for Sausmikat, this is part of the problem. "The AIIB, however, decided against revising this requirement and established a mechanism that is very difficult to access," she stated.

As of January 1, 2026, following two years of external consultations, the AIIB reformed its complaints mechanism. Under certain conditions, complaints can now be filed even while legal proceedings are ongoing.

Sources indicate that but Sausmikat stressed that the changes are insufficient. Of the eight key recommendations made by an independent expert, only three were adopted, she underlined. "The revision did not remove the actual obstacles.".

The AIIB stated that the reforms are intended to make the mechanism "more accessible and responsive.".

The new rules have been in effect for only 10 months, and their implementation is being closely monitored, the bank said.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Steinert stated fear of reprisals poses another fundamental challenge to such procedures.

Documented cases from Latin America, for instance, show that complainants have faced administrative or legal problems, and in some cases even violence.

In a recent development, such risks could deter others from filing complaints, Steinert mentioned. However, his research does not specifically address AIIB projects.

The bank noted that it "does not tolerate retaliation against anyone who raises concerns.".

"Requestors may ask for confidentiality, and the revised PPM policy strengthens protection against reprisals," it added.

Sausmikat stated Germany — as a co-founder and the fourth-largest shareholder of the AIIB — could also play a role, working with other member states to push for changes.

Sources indicate that hartmann also stressed that the bank's shareholders bear responsibility and urged the AIIB's Board of Directors to amend the rules governing the grievance mechanism. "We need a policy based on good-practice standards.".

This article was originally written in German.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While no one has officially confirmed that Mauricio Pochettino is departing the United States men's national team for Manchester United after Michael Carrick's sacking, the faces of Sebastian Berhalter and Folarin Balogun remarked everything that you needed to know at media availability on Thursday ahead of their Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals match with Haiti. With a spot in the Nations League final at stake in this competition, there's a need to be professional during this, and they stressed that, but it was also hard to hide emotions when the manager under whom they experienced some of their best times as USMNT internationals and an entire World Cup is about to depart.

When asked about what he wanted to see, Balogun was succinct, saying, "If I had a vote, I would like to keep things the way they are.".

He continued, saying, "I think things have been working well; we have a clear sense of identity, we have a clear playing style, and whenever you have a top coach, you'd want him to stay, as it's a no-brainer, so I think for us it's no different.".

According to recent reports, it's hard not to feel for Balogun after he became the story of the World Cup for the wrong reasons, with his red card rescinded before he played against Belgium in the round of 16, where the USMNT suffered a 4-1 loss, crashing out of the tournament. Then things went from bad to worse when his move to Everton was called off due to a change in contract terms, and now he is struggling for playing time at Monaco. While he still prepares to leave the French club in January, the national team camp was supposed to be an escape, but instead it has become another uncertain period as Pochettino's days come to an end. Berhalter confirmed that the team hasn't officially heard anything, but that their focus is still on the game at hand.

It has been revealed that "We're focused on going against Haiti twice; they're a good team. You saw at the World Cup, they surprised people, so that's our main focus, and I think the group is ready to play these games," Berhalter noted.

Date: Saturday, Nov. 14 | Time: 4:30 p.m. ETLocation: Nu Stadium -- Miami, FloridaTV: TBS | Live stream: HBO MaxOdds: Haiti +750; Draw +440; USMNT -350.

According to recent reports, berhalter made his national team debut under Pochettino and hasn't looked back, securing 22 caps for the team and making it hard for the Argentine to decide how he should set up the midfield. Because of that, it's hard not to be reflective in uncertain times like these.

In a recent development, "Personally, on the field and off the field, he's done a lot for me, and from day one he's always believed in me. Before I set foot on the field, I think about the way I play and the way that I try to carry myself," Berhalter remarked. "He just said it doesn't matter what you're doing on the field; these are already the right things. And to be honest, I can't thank him enough, and regardless if he's coach, not the coach and, I say it every time that he's meant so much to me. And he's helped me develop as a player and as a person, and as a player, that's all you can ask for: to have that trust and have that belief in you. And for me, it's easy to go out there and just do my job so, he's meant a good deal to me for sure.".

It has been revealed that this is all tough to manage while having games to play. Sure, players will say they're going to be professionals, and these are people who have dealt with stress and needed to maintain that professionalism while doing so, but from a human perspective, it's a well-liked coach leaving on short notice. Even if people anticipated that Pochettino might not make it through to the 2030 World Cup and his departure was a sign that a coach who has done well at the helm was leaving, that doesn't make it any easier on the players. If they go ahead promptly against Haiti on Saturday, they could turn the match into a celebration of what has been so great while playing for Pochettino, but going behind can have a cascading impact where doubt starts to creep in. It's something that the USMNT will need to avoid, even if the future is bright for this squad, no matter who is coaching them.

Pochettino helped raise the standard, and with young players like Cavan Sullivan, Adri Mehmeti, Matias Albert, Neil Pierre and Julian Hall, the future is already here, and no one can feel complacent about their spots. These are things that the fresh coach can bring in, and Pochettino's leadership can set a new standard of what to look for.

Sources indicate that "Yeah, I think the benefit and the blessing when you have a great coach is you know the standard," Balogun said. "I think Poch definitely raised the standard since he's been in charge. I think you guys have seen that, just the intensity of training, how we approach games, he's changed our way of thinking as players, from calling the friendlies that we have in certain camps official games, not official games. He wants us to just be of a mindset to go out there and win.".

Industry observers note that "He's laid the foundation, and I think we, as players, have that ownership to not just do that because Poch was in charge; I think we have the ownership as players to carry that out because we know the standard," he continued. "So yeah, I think that's the benefit of having a top coach, and I'm sure you know whether he's here or not, the US will look to replace him with another top coach.".

Who succeeds Pochettino will be important, but what the players have learned from his time will be invaluable, so the standard can't slip from here. As Balogun stated, it's time to take ownership of their own future because while the coaches may change, the players tasked with leading this team back to the top of Concacaf are already here and understand the task at hand.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026.

Tottenham Hotspur have launched an aggressive campaign to recruit Britain's most talented young footballers from rivals, using expensive private education and lucrative professional contracts to lure them in.

Daily Mail Sport can reveal Spurs are targeting the country's most talented Under 15s through a bespoke package, headed by hefty wages when youngsters turn professional aged 17 and free education at one of the country's finest private schools.

And a glimpse of what the future might look like came against Crystal Palace on October 31.

With Tottenham 2-0 up, Roberto De Zerbi introduced 18-year-old academy graduate Luca Williams-Barnett in the 88th minute. The eye-catching cameo proved a memorable Premier League debut, and last week earned him the top flight's Creative Moment of the Month award for a mazy dribble through Palace's defence.

It's further evidence of the talent coming through at Spurs. Williams-Barnett is not a product of the new recruitment drive, but he offers an illustration of what the club hope to achieve by nurturing talented youngsters and giving them opportunities in the first team.

That has not always been Tottenham's strength, having endured a decade of failing to turn potential into established first-team players. Since Harry Kane and Andros Townsend made their league debuts in 2012, only three Spurs academy graduates – Ryan Mason, Harry Winks and Oliver Skipp – have made at least 30 Premier League appearances for the club.

A glimpse of what Tottenham's future might look like came against Crystal Palace on October 31 with Luca Williams-Barnett's thrilling cameo off the bench.

Since Harry Kane and Andros Townsend (left) made their debuts, only Harry Winks, Ryan Mason (right) and Oliver Skipp have made 30 top-flight appearances from Spurs' academy.

In a Daily Mail Sport interview last month, ex-Spurs player and manager Tim Sherwood claimed Tottenham's inability to give youngsters a proper pathway to the first team has failed those in the set-up over the past decade, and that the academy may as well be 'closed up'.

Industry observers note that it is a record the club are determined to change. Spurs' renewed strategy has been felt across the Premier League's academy circuit over the past year, with rivals anxious at what lies ahead.

In a recent development, the competition for young players is growing. As well as the traditional Big Six clubs, Newcastle, Aston Villa and Brighton have also become worthy competitors because of the first-team pathways they offer.

Sources indicate that tottenham pay £21,000-a-year fees to St John's Senior School in Enfield, which boasts top grades and facilities. Its most recent GCSE cohort achieved 65.3 per cent grades 9–7, formerly known as A* and A grades. The school's football pitch has 22 water cannons underneath (the same number as Arsenal's Emirates Stadium) and both primary and secondary drainage systems.

In a recent development, the programme presented to the parents of prospective stars is the key selling point. Spurs have been given permission by the league to provide a Full-Time Training Module (FTTM) programme which allows students more time away from school. They have their lessons at St John's but on three days a week after lunch, they go to the training ground and focus on football. It is the school's responsibility to organise catch-up lessons so education is not missed out on.

Arsenal, Manchester City, Brighton and Wolves were the first adopters of FTTM, and now Spurs have joined them. Where Tottenham have elevated their strategy is in the number of schoolboys whose fees they cover. Daily Mail Sport understands Spurs have awarded multiple FTTMs to pupils, covering fees in excess of £300,000 annually.

Recent findings suggest that through this, the club have been able to lure in some of the country's best talents. Isaac Allen, who has captained the England Under 15s, joined Spurs from West Ham in August despite Arsenal's attempts to sign him. The 15-year-old struck four goals in three matches at the Under-15 World Cup last month. Gabriel Rigg, 15, was also recruited from West Ham in September, while Spurs beat Arsenal, Chelsea and Newcastle to the signing of Jake Maloney, 14, from Charlton.

The most promising among the cohort is Ashiah Haughton-Sinclair, who in September trained with Spurs' first team. Last season the 15-year-old became the youngest player to feature for their Under 18s, and netted 70 goals and 20 assists.

Troy Parrott (right) came through the youth set-up but struggled for game time behind Kane. He left for AZ Alkmaar in 2024, and this summer signed for Real Betis.

Marcus Edwards (right) is another Spurs academy product who made the grade elsewhere, scoring at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium for Sporting Lisbon in 2022.

Spurs' Hotspur Way base, opened in 2012, is renowned as being one of the finest training complexes in European football, and is regularly used by the England team.

Tottenham's ambitions didn't stop there, as they tried to recruit other players from rivals last summer. The club thought Kyran Thompson was joining from Arsenal, before Newcastle snapped up the talented forward at the last minute. Mishel Nduka, also previously at Arsenal, was approached by Tottenham before he chose a lucrative deal at Manchester City.

Daily Mail Sport understands Spurs pay higher salaries than most Premier League clubs – bar Man City and Chelsea – for academy stars signing professional terms aged 17, which is the earliest age allowed.

This is a significant bargaining chip, as many clubs are rigid in what they will offer players signing their first professional contract.

According to recent reports, there is typically the belief that too much, too young can have a negative impact, but Spurs view it as a necessary ingredient in the modern competition for talent. Nurturing academy graduates into the first team negates the need to spend millions later down the line on established players.

The Tottenham aim is for their first team in the next five years to be reinforced by multiple leading academy graduates, after a decade of producing promising talent – such as Marcus Edwards and Troy Parrott, now at Burnley and Real Betis respectively – without giving them a viable pathway at the club.

Recent findings suggest that and those surplus to requirements could be sold for substantial fees. Luka Vuskovic (£50million to Brighton), Will Lankshear (£20m to Middlesbrough), Ashley Phillips (£20m to Middlesbrough) and Alfie Devine (£6m to Preston North End) are recent examples.

Facilities play a part, too. Spurs' Hotspur Way base, opened in 2012, is renowned as one of the finest training complexes in European football.

The 77-acre state-of-the-art complex in Enfield, which cost £45m to build in 2012 and has since seen significant investment, is home to both the first team and academy, as well as being used regularly by England.

Luka Vuskovic was snapped up before his price tag got too high, and then was sold to Brighton for £50million this summer when he couldn't break into the starting line-up.

Will Lankshear earned Spurs another £20m when he left for Middlesbrough.

With Williams-Barnett already offering a glimpse of what lies ahead, Spurs will hope he is the first of many academy graduates to make the leap.

Sources indicate that while four of the 15 grass pitches are reserved exclusively for first-team training, the youngsters benefit from being immersed in the same elite environment as the senior professionals they aspire to emulate. It's an arrangement designed to make the pathway from youth prospect to Premier League footballer feel that little bit closer.

Timing is everything in football - and that goes for getting transfer moves right, too.

After seven years at Chelsea, Willian made the move across London to join Arsenal in 2020, which seemed like it should be a decent enough fit for all concerned.

But Willian has made no secret of the fact that he did not enjoy his time at the Emirates Stadium - and in hindsight, he believes he may simply have been the wrong player in the wrong place at the wrong time.

In a recent development, willian told FourFourTwo: "These things happen in football. I had some personal frustrations and I couldn't perform on the pitch the way I had been performing at Chelsea.

"Arsenal were also a club that was changing a lot at that time. There were a lot of people leaving and a lot of fresh people coming in.

"It was a restructuring and I got caught up in the middle of it - and it's not easy.

I left a well-established club, winning almost every year, fighting for titles every year, and I joined a club that was trying to find a way to win titles again.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

"So I got caught up in that situation, and that's why things didn't work out. It wasn't easy, but I really wasn't happy.

"The contract I had was actually a very massive one, but it got to the point that money wasn’t enough.

In a recent development, "The most key thing is to be happy, to play with joy. I wasn't able to do so there, so I ended up asking to leave the club, leaving that contract behind.".

After spending a year back in Brazil with Corinthians, Willian found a fresh home at Fulham in 2022 - and he credits Marco Silva with helping him to rediscover his spark.

He noted: "When I left Brazil, my goal was to go to England, stay there, because I love the place and my agent lives there too.

Sources indicate that "Therefore, I decided to be in London, have some meetings and see what the possibilities are. My agent stated, ‘Marco Silva wants to talk to you’. We had a meeting with him, and he invited me to join training and see how I felt.

"It wasn't a trial, it was more to see if I could readjust, especially after what had happened to me at Arsenal.

Sources indicate that "I really liked Marco’s style. I felt celebrated, and it's not flattery, but I felt that respect, that affection from everyone. I was very happy there at Fulham.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The last time FC Barcelona lost a match in the UEFA Women's Champions League was during the 2024-25 UWCL final in Lisbon. Arsenal walked off in Lisbon, Portugal, as Champions League winners and lifted the trophy as Europe's best. On Thursday, Arsenal went into Camp Nou and walked away with a different kind of tournament upset but valuable for their momentum: a 1-1 draw against the current title holders, Barcelona.

Sources indicate that barca's league phase win streak is snapped at three, and Arsenal's efforts lift them inside the top four for the league phase standings. Frida Maanum's goal put the Gunners on the board, while Caroline Graham Hansen equalized for Barcelona. After the final whistle, Arsenal left with the better momentum as matchday five approaches on Nov. 18.

Here's how Arsenal stole the point and Barcelona leveled:.

The visiting side took the game to Barcelona early. Immediately setting the tempo, disrupting the home side's rhythm and turning that into an early chance from Alessia Russo. The moment immediately opened the game up, and Barcelona quickly operated in the final third to record dangerous shots of their own during the opening ten minutes of the match.

Arsenal's Misa Rodriguez stepped up to stop shots, made her shape bigger, and even used her face to block Barcelona's peppering of attempts on target. The team effort to shut out Barcelona in the opening half was an everybody-on-the-pitch approach, with U.S. women's national team defender Emily Fox making a goalkeeping save as well.

WHATEVER IT TAKES 😤Emily Fox and Misa Rodríguez put their bodies on the line for Arsenal 💪Stream every UEFA Women’s Champions League game on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/JqjVCGd8RI.

"I found it hard. I mean, Barcelona is such a good team. Playing them at the Camp Nou, no, is a dream. But the match was a lot of running, a lot of defensive effort from the whole team, top to bottom, but we got the tie," Fox said after the game.

It has been revealed that "I think in the first half, their adjustment, they started to have more rotations out. So I think for us, not being stagnant and really being aggressive and trying our best to keep them out of the pockets and outside the center of the field, that was a significant thing that we talked about. And then from the first half, first on corners and first on blocking shots," Fox explained.

Sometimes the defensive efforts lead to transitional moments of play, and Arsenal's shift in personnel also helped change things in the game.

The group were motivated by the substantial match-up, and got on the scoreboard within the opening 25 minutes of the game. Mariona Caldentey is out with injury, and Frida Maanum's return to the lineup was an immediate game changer. Russo is the club's leading goalscorer this season; she scored a hat-trick against Benfica and is now the leading English goalscorer in the competition's history.

But her efforts against Barcelona helped set up Maanum's opening goal. It was a reminder that the Gunners do have other options even when their main outlet is in top form, and the group carried a narrow one-goal lead into halftime.

FRIDA MAANUM STUNS THE CAMP NOU INTO SILENCE 🤐Arsenal are ahead in Barcelona completely against the run of play 😳Stream every UEFA Women’s Champions League game on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/x3AQAVzm7o.

"I think, you know, the last time we played them, we had some amazing memories, and we knew for them, coming to their place, it was going to be a hard game, and they probably saw it as a rematch, as did we," Fox said.

"So, I think having confidence in our game initiative and each other, knowing that we were going to work for each other no matter what, no matter [the] mistakes, what have you, and during halftime, we just talked about keep doing what we're doing, keep giving them a hard time, keep being aggressive, physical, bumping, and blocking them. And we have 45 minutes to go.".

The second half was as energetic as the opening 45 minutes, and Barcelona increased the urgency even with some players unavailable due to injury. The roster flexed their depth with no Vicky Lopez, Kerolin, or Kika Nazareth, and with Aitana Bonmati only available off the bench.

With her left leg wrapped in medical tape, Caroline Graham Hansen scored the equalizer just before the hour mark.

CAROLINE GRAHAM HANSEN’S ROCKET HAS CAMP NOU ON THEIR FEET AT 1-1 🚀Stream every UEFA Women’s Champions League game on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/0lZEfWJg8f.

"Happy that it's over. But yeah, I'm tired," Graham Hansen joked after the game.

Industry observers note that "No,  it was a game that I feel like we deserve to win. But on the other hand, we also have to give credit to Arsenal. Like, they were there in the last moment to block a lot of shots. Did a good job to be there with us all the way, and to try to make it difficult for us to score. But yeah, on any other given day, I think it's crazy that we don't score more goals on the chances we created today," she mentioned.

Sources indicate that barcelona's 24 shots and seven attempts on target essentially tripled Arsenal's shot total (seven). The other silver lining for the group, other than salvaging a point, is the efforts of their depth players to keep creating in the game.

It has been revealed that "I'm not surprised. I've seen them for a couple of years now, and it was just a matter of time; it was their time to step forward. It was this season, and I was very sure that it would be a matter of confidence," Graham Hansen said about her teammates stepping up.

In a recent development, "And now, when you play more, you get more confidence, and they also take the opportunities they get and show that they're ready, they want to play, and because the quality we knew was there, so I'm not surprised, and I'm just happy for them that they are able to keep showing themselves in the big moments. Because that's what we need, and that's also what they need to keep having the confidence high for the rest of the season.".

#71590. Anthropic IPO: four ways the AI giant wants to disrupt science

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1251 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Anthropic IPO: four ways the AI giant wants to disrupt science

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1251 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Shares in the artificial intelligence firm Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday, in the biggest initial public offering of all time.Credit: Idrees Mohammed/AFP via Getty.
  • Anthropic, the frontier artificial-intelligence organization, has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November.
  • Sources indicate that the maker of AI model Claude, Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a group who broke away from rival giant OpenAI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shares in the artificial intelligence firm Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday, in the biggest initial public offering of all time.Credit: Idrees Mohammed/AFP via Getty.

Anthropic, the frontier artificial-intelligence organization, has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November. With a staggering valuation of around US$1.5 trillion, the firm, based in San Francisco, California, is now among the world’s most valuable companies — and it has major ambitions in science.

Sources indicate that the maker of AI model Claude, Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a group who broke away from rival giant OpenAI. Its models have proven powerful in research, and Anthropic has rolled out its own directed science effort, focusing on areas including quantum mechanics and protein design. This year alone, it has reported mathematics breakthroughs and launched its first life sciences laboratory.

In a recent development, the IPO might also unleash a historic wave of philanthropy: all seven of Anthropic’s founders are likely to become billionaires and have pledged to donate 80% of their equity in the organization to charity, including chief executive Dario Amodei. And on 18 October, the company revealed that it had established the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, created to support initiatives that benefit society and stocked with an initial commitment of 5% of Anthropic’s shares.

But the firm has drawn criticism from researchers, who say its aims of curing diseases on short timescales are unrealistic and that its race towards developing ultra-powerful, ‘superintelligent’ AI models pose serious risks, including an existential threat to humanity. In its public prospectus, published ahead of the IPO, Anthropic outlines a newly introduced governance structure that it notes is “consistent with our commitment to AI safety and responsibility”, and adds that safety research directly shapes the firm’s “model design, training, and deployment.”.

Nature looks at four areas of science where Anthropic is making waves.

According to recent reports, AI’s potential to turbocharge the discovery of latest medicines has been a centerpiece of Anthropic’s pitch to investors. “If today we look at things like cancer, Alzheimer’s, heart disease, mental illness — these will be relics of the past in, I think, less than a decade,” Amodei stated in a promotional video ahead of the IPO.

The company has been rapidly expanding its biomedical ambitions. This year, Anthropic opened its first ‘wet’ laboratory for life sciences research, announced partnerships with several pharmaceutical companies, and noted it was pursuing drug leads of its own. “We plan to scale this work up substantially from here,” the company said on 27 October.

Anthropic bought a one-person, AI-powered biotech: is this drug discovery’s future?

Anthropic bought a one-person, AI-powered biotech: is this drug discovery’s future?

But Amodei’s habit of promising swift, AI-fueled cures for complex diseases has rankled many researchers and entrepreneurs in the field who feel the timeline is unrealistic.

Over the last year, Anthropic has made a major push in the life sciences. In June, the firm hired John Jumper, who shared the 2024 Chemistry Nobel Prize for his work on AlphaFold2 while at Google DeepMind in London.

Some of the tech giant’s early biological research received a mixed reception from biologists. After Anthropic reported using a swarm of AI agents to find signs of a newly introduced CRISPR-like system in viral sequence data, some researchers questioned the novelty of the finding and noted that the company had not carried out the experimental work needed to determine the system’s function.

According to recent reports, in protein design — a field that has boomed thanks to specialist AI tools including AlphaFold — Anthropic’s work has also failed to generate much excitement. In August, Anthropic used Claude Science — an agentic system that can access other biological tools and databases — to make novel ‘binders’ against 15 protein targets.

Recent findings suggest that “Expectations are sky high,” says Anthony Gitter, a computational biologist at the Morgridge Institute for Research in Madison, Wisconsin. “I understand why some view their initial public results as underwhelming.”.

But Gitter is enthusiastic about Anthropic’s protein design efforts, largely because the company was transparent about the work, from the prompts it used to the sequences that were generated. “I would strongly encourage Anthropic to continue that in their future life sciences research,” Gitter adds.

In recent months, Anthropic and other companies — notably Google DeepMind and OpenAI — have been working to establish their research credentials in large part by showing off the rapidly growing mathematical abilities of their flagship AI models.

In a recent development, on 7 September Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge and collaborator Tristan Buckmaster at Latest York University solved a special case of the Navier-Stokes equations, a long-standing problem in mathematical physics that describes the flow of fluids. Hours after Anthropic revealed the result, OpenAI claimed a full solution of the problem, igniting a controversy.

Industry observers note that in another collaboration, Alpöge and mathematical physicist Ethan Sussman at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois, have been working towards establishing the mathematical foundations of the standard model of particle physics. This too is a problem on which OpenAI has made similar claims.

Industry observers note that anthropic and its competitors see the ability to write a rigorous proof of a mathematical fact as a crucial testing ground for their reasoning models. Democracy study: One-quarter of Germans want a right-wing authoritarian dictatorship

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (928 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, satisfaction with democracy in Germany has hit a newly introduced low, while the past is being idealized, and people are expressing a longing for a radical break.
  • The study, led by the Else Frenkel-Brunswik Institute for Democracy Research at the University of Leipzig, is based on the answers to a questionnaire by 2,507 respondents, who the researchers say are a representative cross-section of the German population.
  • For the first time since the study series began, approval of democracy as an idea fell just below the 90% mark, which the study said is primarily attributable to a loss of trust among respondents in the former East Germany (85.7%).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, satisfaction with democracy in Germany has hit a newly introduced low, while the past is being idealized, and people are expressing a longing for a radical break. Antisemitic sentiments and the desire for an authoritarian leader are also on the rise. These are key findings of the authoritarianism study presented Wednesday in Berlin, which has been conducted every two years since 2002.

The study, led by the Else Frenkel-Brunswik Institute for Democracy Research at the University of Leipzig, is based on the answers to a questionnaire by 2,507 respondents, who the researchers say are a representative cross-section of the German population.

For the first time since the study series began, approval of democracy as an idea fell just below the 90% mark, which the study said is primarily attributable to a loss of trust among respondents in the former East Germany (85.7%). The decline in approval of democracy as experienced in everyday life is even more severe: Nationwide, only one-third are satisfied with democracy, with figures having fallen sharply both in eastern (22.8%) and western (36%) states.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The growing rejection of democracy is also reflected in the desire for some kind of authoritarian nationalist government: Just under a quarter of respondents explicitly supported the idea of a "single strong party that embodies the national community as a whole." In the east, the figure stands at 30.9%, above the Germany-wide average of 22.3%.

Industry observers note that "Our democracy is under great pressure. It has lost acceptance among the general population. It is alarming how much an authoritarian yearning is taking its place," concluded social psychologist and study author Oliver Decker.

In a recent development, far-right attitudes have risen for the second consecutive year. Of particular note in the study was what the researchers called a chauvinistic national pride, which, with 19.9% approval, has reached its highest level since the study series began. The proportion of people with a consistently far-right worldview has reached 6.9%, the highest level since 2014, the study found.

Just under 15% of respondents stated they explicitly believe that "everything has to fall apart so that something fresh can emerge," while nearly one in three respondents believes that "something radical is needed for the current state of affairs to change." Another 29.1% agree with this to some extent.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, according to the study, those who share this yearning for catastrophe exhibit significantly stronger antisemitic sentiments — and both are linked to a preference for certain political parties. The study found that a large proportion of eligible voters with this orientation favor the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD).

According to recent reports, "Through its violent rhetoric, the AfD promises to realize the political goals of far-right ideology," the study mentioned. The party's form and content, in other words, correspond exactly to the message that a significant portion of the population wants to hear. "It offers a political home to those who adhere to far-right thinking, while at the same time presenting itself as capable of connecting with a broad segment of society.".

Study co-author Johannes Kiess calls on political leaders at all levels to find countermeasures. "The rejection of the present state of the world must be countered with compelling democratic alternatives and the ability to take political action today," he noted. This also applies to the significant rise in antisemitism, which has more than doubled since 2022.

When asked about the motives behind antisemitic attitudes, the results show that for 16% of respondents, the policies of Israel's government are the decisive factor. This, too, is a record high in the context of the long-term study. While the figure in 2020 was significantly higher in the east (12%) than in the west (8.4%), the figures have since converged. Antisemitism related to Israel is actually slightly stronger in western than in eastern states.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Hostility toward Muslims is also on the rise. It peaked at over 40% in 2018, before dropping to well below 30%, and at the moment stands at 34.1%. These figures are based on two statements respondents were asked to agree with in each survey: "Muslims should be prohibited from immigrating to Germany" and "because of the many Muslims here, I sometimes feel like a stranger in my own country.".

Misogyny is another matter regularly surveyed in the study. In the current survey, 18.3% agreed with anti-feminist statements. Notably, until now, a higher proportion of East Germans had been opposed to feminist causes. As recently as 2024, the difference between the former East (34.6%) and West (19.6%) was enormous. Two years later, the figure in the east has halved to 17.8%, while in western Germany it has fallen only slightly to 18.4%.

Despite the negative trend, there is a glimmer of hope at the end of the Leipzig Authoritarianism Study: While the results are "alarming," long-term trends show that a reversal of this trend is possible: "In earlier surveys, far-right statements already achieved high approval ratings, which then declined again in subsequent years. In addition to the influence of societal crises, political action and its societal perception are of central importance.".

This article was originally written in German. It was first published on November 11 and later edited for clarity.

In a recent development, good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League group stage match between RB Leipzig and Manchester City from Saxony. The hosts started the day in 27th place in the 36-team table after two defeats, both by four goals to one, in away games against Como and Real Madrid. City begin proceedings in 12th after victories over Porto and AEK sandwiching that rip-roaring 4-2 defeat by the champions PSG at the Etihad.

It has been revealed that city, who seemed in rude health after seven successive wins at the start of the Premier League campaign despite the guilty verdicts in the Premier League’s case against them for financial cheating, have wobbled since then, losing their last two league games. Marc Guéhi and Gigi Donnarumma are both suffering bouts of poor form, other individual errors continue to plague them and, although they are creating hatfuls of chances, they have been thwarted by a combination of imprecise finishing and the excellence of Zion Suzuki and Bart Verbruggen.

For all their travails on the road – RB Leipzig have also lost at Werder Bremen, Bayer Leverkusen and Bayern Munich – they have won all their home Bundesliga matches as well as a 1-0 victory over PSV in this competition. Their total of 22 league goals is second only to Bayern’s 27 and Antonio Nusa, a Norway team-mate of Erling Haaland, is in sparkling form flitting behind strikers Christopher Nkunku and Romulo. City, whose full-backs, if you can describe the centre-backs and midfielders who play either side of the centre-halves in that way, never look fit for purpose defensively and may well have their work cut out tonight if he drifts wide.

The Red Bull coaching principles, which have treated us to the dross football of Jesse Marsch, Matthias Jaissle and Ralph Hasenhüttl, all about the long pass, the central channel, counter-pressing and second balls, have a fresh proponent in Martín Demichelis, the forner City and Argentina defender who won the title in 2014 at the Etihad. Three years ago he led River Plate to the title in Argentina, the highlight of a coaching career also spent running Bayern’s U21s, Monterey and Mallorca.

These two have met six times in the last five years, City winning four, most notably the 7-0 thrashing at the Etihad in 2023’s Round of 16, the year they went on to win the Treble. Leipzig’s only victory came at home five years ago in the sixth, redundant group game when City and PSG had already clinched qualification for the knockout stages.

Antoine Semenyo is City’s only absentee; Leipzig will have to do without one-cap Germany midfielder Assan Ouédraogo and former Chelsea striker Marc Guiu.
